words.why: One of the most common words in English. Relying on it makes an essay sound basic, so name the group you really mean.
words.ex: Many people believe that the government should be solely responsible for environmental protection.
words.cloze: Many ___ believe that the government should be solely responsible for environmental protection.

syns.ex: Many individuals believe that the government should be solely responsible for environmental protection.
syns.note: slightly more formal and academic

syns.ex: The public often believes that the government should be solely responsible for environmental protection.
syns.note: people seen as one collective group

syns.ex: Many citizens believe that the government should be solely responsible for environmental protection.
syns.note: ideal for rights, duties and a person's link with their country

drills.plain: People living in rural areas often have less access to healthcare.
drills.cloze: ___ living in rural areas often have less access to healthcare.

drills.plain: People have the right to vote and to express their opinions freely.
drills.cloze: ___ have the right to vote and to express their opinions freely.

words.tip: The strongest upgrade is often to name the group: parents, employers, commuters, young adults.

words.why: You will often argue that a point matters. 'Important' is overused, and a stronger adjective makes the claim more persuasive.
words.ex: It is important for young people to learn a second language.
words.cloze: It is ___ for young people to learn a second language.

syns.ex: It is crucial for young people to learn a second language.
syns.note: a decisive point for future success
syns.hook: Crucial comes from Latin crux, 'cross': a crossroads moment where everything is decided.

syns.ex: It is vital for young people to learn a second language.
syns.note: necessary, even essential for life or success
syns.hook: Vital shares its root with vitamin and vitality (vita = life): you cannot live well without it.

syns.ex: It is essential for young people to learn a second language.
syns.note: a fundamental, necessary component
syns.hook: Essential comes from essence: the very core of something.

drills.plain: Clean drinking water is important for public health.
drills.cloze: Clean drinking water is ___ for public health.

drills.plain: It is important that governments act before the damage becomes permanent.
drills.cloze: It is ___ that governments act before the damage becomes permanent.

words.tip: Pick ONE of these per essay. Using crucial, vital and essential in the same paragraph sounds repetitive.

words.why: 'Good' is vague in academic writing. Examiners reward precision, so say how it is good.
words.ex: Spending time in nature has a good effect on mental health.
words.cloze: Spending time in nature has a ___ effect on mental health.

syns.ex: Spending time in nature has a beneficial effect on mental health.
syns.note: clearly gives an advantage or help

syns.ex: Spending time in nature has a positive effect on mental health.
syns.note: a direct, academic-sounding alternative

syns.ex: Spending time in nature has a favourable effect on mental health.
syns.note: an outcome that is advantageous

drills.plain: Regular exercise has a good influence on students' concentration.
drills.cloze: Regular exercise has a ___ influence on students' concentration.

drills.plain: The new policy had good results for small businesses.
drills.cloze: The new policy had ___ results for small businesses.

words.tip: Say what is good: 'beneficial for health', 'a positive impact on society'.

words.why: A versatile verb for progress, growth and creating something new. Great for solutions, skills and economic change.
words.ex: Countries need to develop more sustainable sources of energy.
words.cloze: Schools should ___ students' critical thinking skills.

syns.ex: Schools should cultivate students' curiosity and critical thinking.
syns.note: suggests gradual, careful development
syns.warn: Pair it with skills, habits and relationships (cultivate a habit). It does not suit physical things like energy sources.
syns.hook: A farmer cultivates a field: patient, careful growth.

syns.ex: Governments should foster innovation in clean energy.
syns.note: encouraging something to grow
syns.warn: Foster goes with ideas and relationships (foster understanding, foster growth), not with physical things.
syns.hook: Foster parents raise someone else's child, so to foster is to nurture something until it grows.

syns.ex: Countries need to establish a national framework for renewable energy.
syns.note: focuses on creating and setting something up

drills.plain: Schools should develop students' critical thinking skills.
drills.cloze: Schools should ___ students' critical thinking skills.

drills.plain: The government plans to develop a national recycling programme.
drills.cloze: The government plans to ___ a national recycling programme.

words.tip: Foster and cultivate go with abstract, people-related things (skills, creativity, relationships). Establish goes with systems and organisations.

words.why: Essential for Task 1 (describing trends) and Task 2 (rising crime, or the need to increase funding).
words.ex: The government plans to increase investment in the public transport system.
words.cloze: The government plans to ___ investment in the public transport system.

syns.ex: The government plans to boost investment in the public transport system.
syns.note: a strong, dynamic word

syns.ex: The government plans to raise investment in the public transport system.
syns.note: lift something to a higher level, often as a new initiative
syns.warn: Raise always takes an object (raise taxes). Rise has none (taxes rise). Don't mix them up.

drills.plain: Free school meals could increase attendance among low-income families.
drills.cloze: Free school meals could ___ attendance among low-income families.

drills.plain: Governments often increase taxes on cigarettes to discourage smoking.
drills.cloze: Governments often ___ taxes on cigarettes to discourage smoking.

words.tip: Boost = stimulate growth. Raise = lift a level, price or awareness.

words.why: A key player in almost every Task 2 topic. You need synonyms so you don't repeat 'the government' in every sentence.
words.ex: The government is responsible for creating policies that protect its citizens.
words.cloze: ___ must create policies that protect ordinary citizens.

syns.ex: The authorities are responsible for creating policies that protect citizens.
syns.note: a general term for the people in power

syns.ex: The state is responsible for creating policies that protect its citizens.
syns.note: the governing body of a nation

syns.ex: Policymakers are responsible for creating policies that protect citizens.
syns.note: the people and groups who write the rules

drills.plain: The government should invest more in renewable energy.
drills.cloze: ___ should invest more in renewable energy.

drills.plain: The government must protect vulnerable groups from exploitation.
drills.cloze: ___ must protect vulnerable groups from exploitation.

words.tip: 'Policymakers' is the best choice when you are talking about decisions and rules, not about running the country.

words.why: This word sits at the heart of questions on social trends, culture and community issues.
words.ex: Modern technology has had a profound impact on society.
words.cloze: Modern technology has had a profound impact on ___.

syns.ex: Modern technology has had a profound impact on the community.
syns.note: society in general, or a more local group

syns.ex: Modern technology has had a profound impact on the general populace.
syns.note: a formal, high-level word for the inhabitants as a whole
syns.warn: Very formal. One use in an essay is plenty.
syns.hook: Populace comes from Latin populus, 'people' (as in population and popular).

syns.ex: Modern technology has had a profound impact on modern civilisation.
syns.note: a broad term for major, long-term historical change
syns.warn: Civilisation means whole cultures across history. It is too big for everyday social issues.
syns.hook: Civil comes from civis, 'citizen': citizens building cities and culture.

drills.plain: Corruption damages society because it erodes trust.
drills.cloze: Corruption damages ___ because it erodes trust.

drills.plain: Great inventions have shaped human society for thousands of years.
drills.cloze: Great inventions have shaped ___ for thousands of years.

words.why: A very frequent topic. Being able to discuss it with varied vocabulary is a real advantage.
words.ex: The advancement of technology has transformed the way we work and communicate.
words.cloze: Rapid ___ can transform the way we work and communicate.

syns.ex: Constant innovation has transformed the way we work and communicate.
syns.note: focuses on new ideas and inventions
syns.warn: Innovation means new ideas and inventions, not technology in general. Use it when you mean 'new'.

syns.ex: Digital tools have transformed the way we work and communicate.
syns.note: more specific: computers, apps and the internet

syns.ex: Technological progress has transformed the way we work and communicate.
syns.note: a good phrase for variety

drills.plain: Technology can help teachers track each student's progress.
drills.cloze: ___ can help teachers track each student's progress.

drills.plain: Without technology, medicine would still be in the dark ages.
drills.cloze: Without ___, medicine would still be in the dark ages.

words.why: Another classic IELTS topic. You need academic language for nature, pollution and conservation.
words.ex: Protecting the environment is a challenge that requires global cooperation.
words.cloze: Protecting ___ is a challenge that requires global cooperation.

syns.ex: Protecting the natural world is a challenge that requires global cooperation.
syns.note: a lovely, descriptive alternative
use: the beauty of the natural world

syns.ex: Protecting our ecosystems is a challenge that requires global cooperation.
syns.note: scientific: complex networks of living things
syns.warn: An ecosystem is a specific network (a reef, a forest), not all of nature.

syns.ex: Protecting the planet is a challenge that requires global cooperation.
syns.note: stresses the global scale

drills.plain: Factories release waste that harms the environment.
drills.cloze: Factories release waste that harms ___.

drills.plain: Many people feel a duty to protect the environment for future generations.
drills.cloze: Many people feel a duty to protect ___ for future generations.

words.why: Education, family and social development are common themes, so you need alternatives to 'children'.
words.ex: It is vital that children are taught about healthy eating habits from a young age.
words.cloze: It is vital that ___ are taught about healthy eating habits from a young age.

syns.ex: It is vital that youngsters are taught about healthy eating habits.
syns.note: slightly less formal, but acceptable in IELTS speaking

syns.ex: It is vital that the youth are taught about healthy eating habits.
syns.note: the whole age group, as a demographic
syns.warn: 'The youth' is a group. For individuals say 'a young person'.

syns.ex: It is vital that minors are taught about healthy eating habits.
syns.note: a formal, legal-sounding term, good for law and responsibility
syns.hook: Minor means lesser: lesser in age in the eyes of the law.

drills.plain: Governments should limit junk-food advertising aimed at children.
drills.cloze: Governments should limit junk-food advertising aimed at ___.

drills.plain: Children today spend far more time on screens than earlier generations did.
drills.cloze: ___ today spend far more time on screens than earlier generations did.

words.tip: Context decides. Use the exact age word when it helps.

words.why: Essential for any education essay, from primary school to university.
words.ex: Universities should provide more mental health support for their students.
words.cloze: Universities should provide more mental health support for their ___.

syns.ex: Universities should provide more mental health support for their learners.
syns.note: a broader term that focuses on the process of studying

syns.ex: Schools should provide more support for their pupils.
syns.note: usually school-age children, not university students

syns.ex: The university provides funding for its most promising scholars.
syns.note: high-achieving academic students, often at a higher level
syns.warn: Scholars are serious researchers or award-winners, not ordinary students.
syns.hook: Scholar comes from Latin schola, 'school': someone who studies seriously.

drills.plain: Primary-school students need short, active and playful lessons.
drills.cloze: Primary-school ___ need short, active and playful lessons.

drills.plain: Online platforms help students study at their own pace.
drills.cloze: Online platforms help ___ study at their own pace.

words.why: A core verb for solutions and for talking about positive developments.
words.ex: Governments must take steps to improve air quality in major cities.
words.cloze: Governments must take steps to ___ air quality in major cities.

syns.ex: Governments must take steps to enhance air quality in major cities.
syns.note: raise or intensify the quality of something

syns.ex: Governments must take steps to ameliorate the problem of poor air quality.
syns.note: a high-level, formal word: make something bad better
syns.warn: Very formal and rare. It means to make a bad situation less bad. Don't use it unless you are sure.
syns.hook: Ameliorate comes from Latin melior, 'better': a-MEEL-yuh-rate.

syns.ex: The company sought to refine its manufacturing process to reduce waste.
syns.note: improve through small changes

drills.plain: New housing schemes aim to improve living conditions in poorer districts.
drills.cloze: New housing schemes aim to ___ living conditions in poorer districts.

drills.plain: The company decided to improve its production process to cut waste.
drills.cloze: The company decided to ___ its production process to cut waste.

words.tip: Enhance = raise quality. Refine = tweak what already works.

words.why: When you propose a solution in Task 2, you argue that it will be 'effective'. A range of words shows better command of English.
words.ex: Stricter penalties are an effective deterrent to crime.
words.cloze: Stricter penalties have proved ___ in reducing crime.

syns.ex: The two sides held a productive discussion about reducing crime.
syns.note: gets useful results, especially in talks and teamwork
syns.warn: Productive suits discussions, meetings, partnerships and workers. It is not a natural partner for laws or penalties (not 'a productive deterrent').

syns.ex: Stricter penalties are a potent deterrent to crime.
syns.note: powerful, with a strong effect
syns.warn: Potent means powerful (a potent drug, a potent image). It sounds odd after 'in doing'.
syns.hook: Potent shares a root with potential and power.

syns.ex: Stricter penalties have proved successful in reducing crime.
syns.note: focuses on the positive outcome

drills.plain: Stricter laws on drink-driving have been effective.
drills.cloze: Stricter laws on drink-driving have been ___.

drills.plain: A single effective image can change public attitudes.
drills.cloze: A single ___ image can change public attitudes.

words.why: Used to say something is required. A strong way to frame a solution or a duty.
words.ex: It is necessary for individuals to take personal responsibility for their health.
words.cloze: It is ___ for individuals to take personal responsibility for their health.

syns.ex: It is essential for individuals to take personal responsibility for their health.
syns.note: absolutely required, fundamental

syns.ex: It is imperative that individuals take personal responsibility for their health.
syns.note: very strong and formal, with a sense of urgency
syns.hook: Imperative comes from Latin imperare, 'to command' (like emperor): it commands action.

drills.plain: It is necessary that governments act now.
drills.cloze: It is ___ that governments act now.

drills.plain: Basic literacy is necessary for almost every job.
drills.cloze: Basic literacy is ___ for almost every job.

words.tip: Imperative is for urgency. Use it once, in a conclusion or a strong recommendation.

words.why: Useful for comparison and contrast, a key skill in academic writing.
words.ex: There are many different approaches to solving this problem.
words.cloze: There are ___ approaches to solving this problem.

syns.ex: There are various approaches to solving this problem.
syns.note: very common and effective

syns.ex: There are diverse approaches to solving this problem.
syns.note: emphasises a wide range of distinct types

drills.plain: Students from different backgrounds enrich classroom discussion.
drills.cloze: Students from ___ backgrounds enrich classroom discussion.

drills.plain: There are many different ways to reduce stress.
drills.cloze: There are ___ ways to reduce stress.

words.tip: Don't say 'many various'. Say 'various approaches' or 'a variety of approaches'.

words.why: Work, careers and employment are frequent topics.
words.ex: Finding fulfilling work is a major goal for many young adults.
words.cloze: Many young adults want to pursue a fulfilling ___.

syns.ex: Finding fulfilling employment is a major goal for many young adults.
syns.note: a more formal term

syns.ex: Building a fulfilling career is a major goal for many young adults.
syns.note: a long-term professional journey

syns.ex: Entering a fulfilling profession is a major goal for many young adults.
syns.note: a job that needs special training, like medicine or law

drills.plain: Rising automation threatens work for low-skilled workers.
drills.cloze: Rising automation threatens ___ for low-skilled workers.

drills.plain: Doctors and lawyers belong to highly respected jobs.
drills.cloze: Doctors and lawyers belong to highly respected ___.

words.tip: Work is uncountable. Say 'work', not 'a work' or 'works', when you mean a job.

words.why: Essential for business, the economy, globalisation and marketing topics.
words.ex: Companies have a social responsibility to minimise their environmental impact.
words.cloze: ___ have a social responsibility to minimise their environmental impact.

syns.ex: Corporations have a social responsibility to minimise their environmental impact.
syns.note: typically large companies

syns.ex: Businesses have a social responsibility to minimise their environmental impact.
syns.note: a general term for any commercial organisation

drills.plain: Large companies can afford to invest in clean technology.
drills.cloze: Large ___ can afford to invest in clean technology.

drills.plain: Many small companies struggle to survive in their first two years.
drills.cloze: Many small ___ struggle to survive in their first two years.

words.why: Already a formal, academic word for 'person', used to discuss personal responsibility and rights. The guide's two alternatives are for variety, not an upgrade.
words.ex: The rights of the individual must be balanced against the needs of the community.
words.cloze: The rights of the ___ must be balanced against the needs of the community.

syns.ex: The rights of each person must be balanced against the needs of the community.
syns.note: the singular, everyday word
syns.warn: Less formal than 'individual'. Fine, but it won't lift your vocabulary score.

syns.ex: The rights of the citizen must be balanced against the needs of the community.
syns.note: stresses the person's role within a state
syns.warn: Only when you mean a person in relation to their country. Otherwise it changes the meaning.

drills.plain: Each individual should take responsibility for reducing waste.
drills.cloze: Each ___ should take responsibility for reducing waste.

drills.plain: Taxes fund services that benefit every individual in the country.
drills.cloze: Taxes fund services that benefit every ___ in the country.

words.tip: 'Individual' is already a strong word. Keep it for 'the individual versus the community' contrasts.

words.why: Environment, economy and culture are often discussed on a global scale, so this adjective is crucial.
words.ex: Climate change is a global issue that requires an international response.
words.cloze: Climate change is a ___ problem that needs shared solutions.

syns.ex: Climate change is a worldwide issue that requires an international response.
syns.note: a direct, perfectly suitable synonym

syns.ex: Climate change is an international issue that requires cooperation.
syns.note: involving two or more nations

syns.ex: The desire for peace is a universal human trait.
syns.note: applying to everyone, everywhere
syns.hook: Universal comes from universe: the whole of everything.

drills.plain: Air pollution has become a global concern.
drills.cloze: Air pollution has become ___ concern.

drills.plain: Access to clean water should be a global right.
drills.cloze: Access to clean water should be ___ right.

words.why: Used to contrast the present with the past. A key word for social change, tradition and technology essays.
words.ex: Modern lifestyles are often more sedentary than those of previous generations.
words.cloze: ___ lifestyles are often more sedentary than those of previous generations.

syns.ex: Contemporary lifestyles are often more sedentary than those of previous generations.
syns.note: a more formal, academic-sounding synonym
syns.warn: Contemporary can also mean 'from the same period' (contemporary accounts of the war).

syns.ex: Present-day lifestyles are often more sedentary than those of previous generations.
syns.note: clear and effective

drills.plain: Modern architects often use recycled materials.
drills.cloze: ___ architects often use recycled materials.

drills.plain: Modern technology has made long-distance communication easy.
drills.cloze: ___ technology has made long-distance communication easy.

words.why: A very common quantifier. It is fine, but relying on it can feel repetitive, and alternatives add academic flair.
words.ex: Many experts argue that automation will lead to job losses.
words.cloze: ___ experts argue that automation will lead to job losses.

syns.ex: Numerous experts argue that automation will lead to job losses.
syns.note: a direct, formal synonym

syns.ex: A large number of experts argue that automation will lead to job losses.
syns.note: a simple, effective phrase for variety
syns.warn: Only with countable nouns. Use 'a large amount of' with uncountables.

drills.plain: Many studies link sugary drinks to obesity.
drills.cloze: ___ studies link sugary drinks to obesity.

drills.plain: Many students struggle to find affordable housing.
drills.cloze: ___ students struggle to find affordable housing.

words.why: A simple, common verb. In formal writing a more sophisticated alternative sounds more authoritative.
words.ex: Volunteering can help students develop a sense of responsibility.
words.cloze: Volunteering can ___ students in developing a sense of responsibility.

syns.ex: Volunteering can assist students in developing a sense of responsibility.
syns.note: a more formal alternative

syns.ex: Volunteering can aid the development of a student's sense of responsibility.
syns.note: another formal choice, often used with 'in' or as a noun

syns.ex: Volunteering can support students in developing a sense of responsibility.
syns.note: providing a foundation or encouragement

drills.plain: Community centres help older people to stay active.
drills.cloze: Community centres ___ older people to stay active.

drills.plain: Early diagnosis can help recovery.
drills.cloze: Early diagnosis can ___ recovery.

words.why: A strong academic verb for giving, supplying or making something available. Excellent for solution paragraphs.
words.ex: Libraries provide access to a vast range of information for free.
words.cloze: Charities ___ food and shelter to homeless people.

syns.ex: Charities supply food and blankets to flood victims.
syns.note: a direct synonym that implies meeting a need

syns.ex: Libraries offer access to a vast range of information for free.
syns.note: makes something available to take or leave

syns.ex: The report furnishes clear evidence that exercise improves memory.
syns.note: a more formal, high-level verb meaning to supply
syns.warn: Rare. It needs the pattern 'furnish SOMEONE with SOMETHING'.
syns.hook: Furnish a room means to fill it with what is needed; furnishing someone with facts fills their need.

drills.plain: Governments should provide affordable housing for low-income families.
drills.cloze: Governments should ___ affordable housing for low-income families.

drills.plain: The museum provides visitors with free audio guides.
drills.cloze: The museum ___ visitors with free audio guides.

words.why: Used to introduce an opinion. Alternatives show conviction and add academic weight to your claims.
words.ex: I believe that censorship in the media is sometimes justified.
words.cloze: I would ___ that censorship in the media is sometimes justified.

syns.ex: I would argue that censorship in the media is sometimes justified.
syns.note: stronger: suggests you have reasons and evidence

syns.ex: Some contend that censorship in the media is sometimes justified.
syns.note: a formal verb for putting forward an argument
syns.hook: Contend is to fight for a point (a contest of ideas).

drills.plain: Some people believe that standardised exams measure memory rather than ability.
drills.cloze: Some people ___ that standardised exams measure memory rather than ability.

drills.plain: I believe that cities should ban cars from their centres.
drills.cloze: I ___ that cities should ban cars from their centres.

words.tip: Mix your openers: 'I would argue that…', 'It could be contended that…', 'Some people hold that…'.

words.why: A powerful verb for making something exist, from jobs and opportunities to policies and art.
words.ex: The government should implement policies to create more jobs for young graduates.
words.cloze: The government should implement policies to ___ more jobs for young graduates.

syns.ex: The government should implement policies to generate more jobs for young graduates.
syns.note: often used for jobs, revenue or electricity

syns.ex: The government should establish a programme to create more jobs.
syns.note: setting something up on a firm, long-term basis

drills.plain: Wind farms create electricity without burning fossil fuels.
drills.cloze: Wind farms ___ electricity without burning fossil fuels.

drills.plain: The city plans to create a fund for young start-ups.
drills.cloze: The city plans to ___ a fund for young start-ups.

words.why: A core IELTS topic. You need a range of words to discuss it without repeating yourself.
words.ex: Access to quality education is crucial for a nation's progress.
words.cloze: Access to quality ___ is crucial for a nation's progress.

syns.ex: Access to quality schooling is crucial for a nation's progress.
syns.note: the formal teaching a child receives in classrooms

syns.ex: Lifelong learning is crucial for personal and professional development.
syns.note: a broader idea, including self-study and experience

drills.plain: Education should prepare young people for the world of work.
drills.cloze: ___ should prepare young people for the world of work.

drills.plain: Education does not stop after graduation. It is a lifelong process.
drills.cloze: ___ does not stop after graduation. It is a lifelong process.

words.why: Another central IELTS topic, covering diet, exercise and healthcare systems.
words.ex: An individual's diet has a direct impact on their overall health.
words.cloze: An individual's diet has a direct impact on their overall ___.

syns.ex: An individual's diet has a direct impact on their overall well-being.
syns.note: broader: includes mental and social health, not just physical

syns.ex: An individual's diet has a direct impact on their physical condition.
syns.note: more specific to the body

syns.ex: The government needs to invest more in public healthcare.
syns.note: the system that provides medical services
syns.warn: Healthcare is the system of services. It is not a person's state of health.

drills.plain: Long working hours can damage workers' health.
drills.cloze: Long working hours can damage workers' ___.

drills.plain: Governments must invest more in health services.
drills.cloze: Governments must invest more in ___ services.

words.why: A fundamental social unit and a common topic for society, tradition and child-development questions.
words.ex: The family structure has changed significantly over the last 50 years.
words.cloze: ___ size has fallen sharply over the last 50 years.

syns.ex: The average household now contains fewer people than it did 50 years ago.
syns.note: the people living together in one home

syns.ex: The domestic unit has changed significantly over the last 50 years.
syns.note: a very formal, sociological term for family or household
syns.warn: Avoid it in IELTS essays. It is an unusual phrase even in sociology, where 'household' is the standard term.

drills.plain: Families on low incomes are struggling with energy bills.
drills.cloze: ___ on low incomes are struggling with energy bills.

drills.plain: In the 1950s, the family was typically centred on a single breadwinner.
drills.cloze: In the 1950s, ___ was typically centred on a single breadwinner.

words.why: Essential vocabulary for any education essay.
words.ex: Good teachers are essential for a positive learning environment.
words.cloze: Good ___ are essential for a positive learning environment.

syns.ex: Good educators are essential for a positive learning environment.
syns.note: a broader, more formal term

syns.ex: Many students hire private tutors to help them with difficult subjects.
syns.note: teaches individuals or small groups

syns.ex: Driving instructors must be patient and clear.
syns.note: often someone who teaches a practical skill

drills.plain: Many parents hire teachers to help their children with maths.
drills.cloze: Many parents hire ___ to help their children with maths.

drills.plain: Flight teachers must hold a special licence.
drills.cloze: Flight ___ must hold a special licence.

words.why: Used to discuss people who are no longer children. Essential for education, work and life-stage essays.
words.ex: Many adults are now returning to university to gain new qualifications.
words.cloze: Many ___ are now returning to university to gain new qualifications.

syns.ex: Many grown-ups are now returning to university.
syns.note: slightly less formal but widely understood
syns.warn: Informal. Fine in speaking, but 'adults' is safer in writing.

syns.ex: Mature individuals often have different learning needs compared with younger students.
syns.note: a formal and respectful way to refer to adults

drills.plain: Adults often find it harder to learn languages than children do.
drills.cloze: ___ often find it harder to learn languages than children do.

drills.plain: Some adults still rely on their parents financially.
drills.cloze: Some ___ still rely on their parents financially.

words.why: A key adjective for anything to do with society, community and interaction between people.
words.ex: The rise of social media has had a major impact on people's social lives.
words.cloze: Rapid urbanisation has changed ___ norms in many countries.

syns.ex: The flats have a communal garden shared by all the residents.
syns.note: shared by everyone in a group
syns.warn: Communal means shared by a group (communal kitchen). It is not a general synonym for 'social'.

syns.ex: Societal norms have changed dramatically in recent decades.
syns.note: a very formal adjective about how people in general live together

syns.ex: His behaviour in a public setting was unacceptable.
syns.note: relating to people in general
syns.warn: Public is not a general replacement for social. Keep 'social' in fixed phrases (social media, social skills, social class).

drills.plain: Loneliness is a growing social problem.
drills.cloze: Loneliness is a growing ___ problem.

drills.plain: Villages often share social spaces such as wells and meeting halls.
drills.cloze: Villages often share ___ spaces such as wells and meeting halls.

words.why: Describes services and spaces for everyone, often provided by the government.
words.ex: Investment in public transport is essential to reduce traffic congestion.
words.cloze: Investment in ___ transport is essential to reduce traffic congestion.

syns.ex: Investment in state-run transport is essential to reduce traffic congestion.
syns.note: managed by the government itself

syns.ex: Investment in state-funded services is essential.
syns.note: paid for out of taxes

syns.ex: Civic duty includes voting and respecting the law.
syns.note: relating to a town or city and citizens' duties
syns.warn: Use it only in fixed phrases such as civic duty, civic pride and civic engagement.

syns.ex: The community swimming pool is open to everyone.
syns.note: provided for the people of one local area
syns.warn: Community works as a modifier only in set phrases (community centre, community service). It is not a general replacement for 'public'.

drills.plain: Many people rely on public libraries for free internet access.
drills.cloze: Many people rely on ___ libraries for free internet access.

drills.plain: Voting is an important part of our public duty.
drills.cloze: Voting is an important part of our ___ duty.

words.why: An adjective for a particular area, neighbourhood or region, often in contrast to 'national' or 'global'.
words.ex: Supporting local businesses is beneficial for the community's economy.
words.cloze: To keep money circulating in the town, residents should support ___ businesses.

syns.ex: Supporting community-based businesses is beneficial.
syns.note: run by and for the people of one area

syns.ex: The neighbourhood watch scheme helped to reduce crime.
syns.note: a specific residential area

syns.ex: Supporting regional businesses is beneficial for the area's economy.
syns.note: a larger area than a single town
syns.warn: Regional covers a larger area than a town. Don't use it if you mean one neighbourhood.

drills.plain: Local newspapers keep residents informed about council decisions.
drills.cloze: ___ newspapers keep residents informed about council decisions.

drills.plain: A local accent can differ even between nearby towns.
drills.cloze: A ___ accent can differ even between nearby towns.

words.why: An abstract idea at the centre of many essays (free time, change over time). You often need phrases instead of one-word synonyms.
words.ex: People today seem to have less free time than in the past.
words.cloze: People today seem to have fewer ___ than in the past.

syns.ex: People today seem to have fewer leisure hours than in the past.
syns.note: specifically time that is not work

syns.ex: In a bygone era, people had more free time.
syns.note: a distinct period in history

drills.plain: Parents rarely have free time on weekdays.
drills.cloze: Parents rarely have ___ on weekdays.

drills.plain: Life was simpler in that period.
drills.cloze: Life was simpler in ___.

words.why: A very broad word. Making it more specific shows a higher level of language skill.
words.ex: Technology has changed almost every aspect of modern life.
words.cloze: Technology has changed almost every aspect of modern ___.

syns.ex: Technology has changed almost every aspect of modern existence.
syns.note: more philosophical and formal
syns.warn: Sounds abstract. Don't use it for everyday topics.

syns.ex: Technology has changed almost every aspect of modern lifestyles.
syns.note: the manner in which people live

syns.ex: Technology has changed the daily routines of most people.
syns.note: specific to day-to-day activities

drills.plain: Smartphones have transformed life in rural areas.
drills.cloze: Smartphones have transformed ___ in rural areas.

drills.plain: Philosophers have long asked about the meaning of life.
drills.cloze: Philosophers have long asked about the meaning of ___.

words.why: It can mean an event you lived through or, more often in IELTS, the knowledge and skill gained from doing something.
words.ex: Most employers look for candidates with practical work experience.
words.cloze: Most employers look for candidates with ___ in the field.

syns.ex: Most employers look for candidates with practical knowledge.
syns.note: highlights the hands-on side

syns.ex: Most employers look for candidates with expertise in the field.
syns.note: a stronger word for a high level of skill
syns.hook: Expertise comes from expert, 'tried and tested' through long practice.

drills.plain: Interns gain valuable experience before they apply for full-time jobs.
drills.cloze: Interns gain valuable ___ before they apply for full-time jobs.

drills.plain: Hospitals need staff with specialised experience in emergency care.
drills.cloze: Hospitals need staff with specialised ___ in emergency care.

words.why: Absolutely essential for education and employment topics.
words.ex: The education system should focus on teaching practical skills as well as academic knowledge.
words.cloze: The education system should focus on teaching practical ___ as well as academic knowledge.

syns.ex: The education system should focus on teaching practical abilities.
syns.note: a general synonym

syns.ex: The education system should focus on developing core competencies.
syns.note: a formal, business word for skills needed to do a job

syns.ex: He was admired for his academic prowess.
syns.note: a high-level word for great skill or expertise
syns.warn: Prowess is uncountable and means admired excellence. It rarely suits 'practical' skills.
syns.hook: Prowess is admirable skill, like a brave knight's.

drills.plain: Employers value communication skills above technical ones.
drills.cloze: Employers value communication ___ above technical ones.

drills.plain: The team was admired for its skill in negotiations.
drills.cloze: The team was admired for its ___ in negotiations.

words.why: Central to discussions about media, the internet and education.
words.ex: The internet allows for the instant sharing of information across the globe.
words.cloze: The internet allows for the instant sharing of ___ across the globe.

syns.ex: The internet allows for the instant sharing of data across the globe.
syns.note: often raw facts, figures and statistics

syns.ex: The internet allows for the instant sharing of knowledge across the globe.
syns.note: information that is understood and organised

drills.plain: Companies collect information about customers' shopping habits.
drills.cloze: Companies collect ___ about customers' shopping habits.

drills.plain: Universities exist to pass on information from one generation to the next.
drills.cloze: Universities exist to pass on ___ from one generation to the next.

words.why: A group of people living in the same place or sharing a characteristic.
words.ex: Public libraries can be a vital hub for the local community.
words.cloze: Public libraries can be a vital hub for the local ___.

syns.ex: Public libraries are vital for a well-functioning society.
syns.note: broader: the people of a country or region

syns.ex: The local populace can benefit from public libraries.
syns.note: a formal word for the inhabitants of an area
syns.warn: It sounds literary or journalistic. 'Residents' or 'the population' is usually the safer choice.
syns.hook: Populace comes from Latin populus, 'people' (as in population and popular).

syns.ex: A public library can be a vital hub for the neighbourhood.
syns.note: specific to a residential area

drills.plain: Parks improve quality of life for the whole community.
drills.cloze: Parks improve quality of life for the whole ___.

drills.plain: A strong community protects its most vulnerable members.
drills.cloze: A strong ___ protects its most vulnerable members.

words.why: A crucial adjective for the economy, finance, trade and business.
words.ex: The government's main goal is to promote economic growth.
words.cloze: The central bank aims to maintain ___ stability.

syns.ex: The government's main goal is to ensure financial stability.
syns.note: relating to money management
syns.warn: Economic is about the economy (growth, trade). Financial is about money and banking. Don't swap them blindly.

syns.ex: The central bank sets monetary policy, such as interest rates.
syns.note: specifically about the money supply of a country
syns.hook: Monetary comes from Latin moneta, the Roman temple where coins were made.

drills.plain: Many students face economic pressure during their studies.
drills.cloze: Many students face ___ pressure during their studies.

drills.plain: Interest rates are a key tool of economic policy.
drills.cloze: Interest rates are a key tool of ___ policy.

words.why: Describes something that relates to or affects a single person. Used to contrast with 'public' or 'general'.
words.ex: The choice to have children is a deeply personal decision.
words.cloze: The choice to have children is a deeply ___ decision.

syns.ex: The choice to have children is a deeply individual decision.
syns.note: a direct, formal synonym

syns.ex: The choice to have children is a private matter.
syns.note: stresses that it is not for public interference

syns.ex: Art appreciation is a highly subjective experience.
syns.note: based on personal feelings, not facts
syns.hook: Subjective means it depends on the subject, the person, and their feelings.

drills.plain: Religion is a personal matter, and the state should not interfere.
drills.cloze: Religion is a ___ matter, and the state should not interfere.

drills.plain: Judging art is personal: there is no single correct answer.
drills.cloze: Judging art is ___: there is no single correct answer.

words.why: Describes something that relates to a whole nation, as opposed to local or global.
words.ex: The country's national identity is built on its unique history and culture.
words.cloze: The government launched a ___ vaccination campaign covering every region of the country.

syns.ex: The government announced a nationwide lockdown.
syns.note: covering every part of the country

syns.ex: Domestic policy focuses on issues within the country.
syns.note: inside the country, as opposed to foreign or international
syns.warn: Domestic can also mean 'of the home' (domestic chores).

drills.plain: A national strike left airports closed across the country.
drills.cloze: A ___ strike left airports closed across the country.

drills.plain: National policy should focus on problems inside the country first.
drills.cloze: ___ policy should focus on problems inside the country first.

words.why: More powerful and academic than 'important' or 'big'. It means large or important enough to be worth attention.
words.ex: There has been a significant increase in the use of renewable energy.
words.cloze: There has been a ___ increase in the use of renewable energy.

syns.ex: There has been a substantial increase in the use of renewable energy.
syns.note: suggests a large amount or size
syns.hook: Substance means real weight: a substantial rise is not a small one.

syns.ex: There has been a considerable increase in the use of renewable energy.
syns.note: another strong word for a large amount

syns.ex: There has been a marked increase in the use of renewable energy.
syns.note: noticeable and clear
syns.hook: A mark stands out: a marked change is easy to see.

drills.plain: Smoking rates have fallen by a significant margin.
drills.cloze: Smoking rates have fallen by a ___ margin.

drills.plain: There was a significant difference between the two groups.
drills.cloze: There was a ___ difference between the two groups.

words.tip: Great in Task 1 for trends: 'a marked rise', 'a considerable fall'.

words.why: Used to say whether something can be done. Key for solutions in Task 2.
words.ex: It is possible to reduce pollution if we take collective action.
words.cloze: It is ___ to reduce pollution if we take collective action.

syns.ex: It is feasible to reduce pollution if we take collective action.
syns.note: possible and practical to do
syns.hook: Feasible comes from French faire, 'to do': it can be done.

syns.ex: This is not a financially viable solution.
syns.note: capable of working successfully, often in business
syns.hook: Viable comes from vita, 'life': able to survive on its own.

syns.ex: Setting attainable goals is key to motivation.
syns.note: able to be reached or achieved
syns.hook: Attain means to reach: attainable is within reach.

drills.plain: A four-day working week is possible for many offices.
drills.cloze: A four-day working week is ___ for many offices.

drills.plain: Solar power has become a possible alternative to coal.
drills.cloze: Solar power has become a ___ alternative to coal.

words.why: Advanced vocabulary for high-impact writing, in the guide's last group of six words.
words.ex: Not enough funding is available for arts and culture.
words.cloze: Higher education should be ___ to everyone, regardless of income.

syns.ex: Higher education should be accessible to everyone, regardless of income.
syns.note: it is easy to get or use

syns.ex: Reliable data is not always obtainable in remote regions.
syns.note: a formal word for 'able to be got'
syns.warn: Uncommon. 'Available' is usually more natural, so use it sparingly.
syns.hook: Obtain means to get, so obtainable means gettable.

syns.ex: We need to use the resources we have on hand.
syns.note: present and ready for use
syns.warn: Fairly informal. Fine in speaking; in writing prefer 'available'.

drills.plain: Healthy food should be available to everyone, not only the wealthy.
drills.cloze: Healthy food should be ___ to everyone, not only the wealthy.

drills.plain: Paramedics are always available at large events.
drills.cloze: Paramedics are always ___ at large events.

words.why: Advanced vocabulary for high-impact writing.
words.ex: Traffic congestion is a common problem in most major cities.
words.cloze: Traffic congestion is a ___ problem in most major cities.

syns.ex: Traffic congestion is a widespread problem in most major cities.
syns.note: found over a large area

syns.ex: Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern society.
syns.note: present or found everywhere
syns.warn: Strong: use it only when something really is everywhere.
syns.hook: Ubi is Latin for 'where': ubiquitous means 'everywhere you look'.

syns.ex: Car accidents are a frequent occurrence on this road.
syns.note: happening often

drills.plain: Smartphones are now common in classrooms around the world.
drills.cloze: Smartphones are now ___ in classrooms around the world.

drills.plain: Delays on this railway line are common.
drills.cloze: Delays on this railway line are ___.

words.why: Advanced vocabulary for high-impact writing.
words.ex: The campaign to raise awareness about recycling was very successful.
words.cloze: The recycling campaign was highly ___.

syns.ex: The discussion was very fruitful, and we came up with many new ideas.
syns.note: produces good results
syns.hook: Fruit is what a plant produces; fruitful work produces results.

syns.ex: The business became very prosperous.
syns.note: financial success or flourishing in general
syns.hook: Prosperous comes from Latin spes, 'hope': things turned out as hoped.

syns.ex: The company is thriving in the current market.
syns.note: growing and developing vigorously
syns.hook: A thriving plant grows strong and healthy.

drills.plain: The small bakery became a successful business within two years.
drills.cloze: The small bakery became a ___ business within two years.

drills.plain: Years of trade made the port city successful.
drills.cloze: Years of trade made the port city ___.

words.why: Advanced vocabulary for high-impact writing.
words.ex: The general opinion is that taxes are too high.
words.cloze: The ___ opinion is that taxes are too high.

syns.ex: The overall opinion is that taxes are too high.
syns.note: considering everything

syns.ex: There is broad agreement that taxes are too high.
syns.note: wide in scope, covering many views

syns.ex: There is widespread agreement that taxes are too high.
syns.note: held by many people

syns.ex: The prevailing opinion is that taxes are too high.
syns.note: existing at a particular time, current
syns.hook: Prevailing comes from prevail: the view that wins out right now.

drills.plain: There is general support for the new law.
drills.cloze: There is ___ support for the new law.

drills.plain: Despite some delays, the general result was positive.
drills.cloze: Despite some delays, the ___ result was positive.

words.why: Advanced vocabulary for high-impact writing.
words.ex: Streaming services have become extremely popular in recent years.
words.cloze: Streaming services have become ___ in recent years.

syns.ex: The use of streaming services has become widespread.
syns.note: found over a large area or among many people

syns.ex: This belief is more prevalent among younger generations.
syns.note: widespread in a particular area or at a particular time
syns.warn: 'Popular' means liked. Widespread and prevalent mean common. The meaning shifts slightly, so check it still says what you mean.
syns.hook: Prevalent shares a root with prevail: the thing that has won out is the one found everywhere.

drills.plain: Remote work has become more popular since 2020.
drills.cloze: Remote work has become more ___ since 2020.

drills.plain: Online shopping is popular among older adults.
drills.cloze: Online shopping is ___ among older adults.

words.why: Advanced vocabulary for high-impact writing: comparatives that sound more academic.
words.ex: We need to put more effort into protecting the environment.
words.cloze: We need to put ___ effort into protecting the environment.

syns.ex: We need to put greater effort into protecting the environment.
syns.note: a more formal and emphatic choice

syns.ex: We need to provide additional funding for schools.
syns.note: adds to what is already there

syns.ex: Further research is needed to confirm these findings.
syns.note: often used for abstract things like research, details or thought

drills.plain: Schools need more funding to reduce class sizes.
drills.cloze: Schools need ___ funding to reduce class sizes.

drills.plain: More studies are needed to confirm these results.
drills.cloze: ___ studies are needed to confirm these results.

contexts.stem: The ___ at the local primary school wear blue uniforms.
contexts.why: Pupils are usually school-age children. Scholars are serious academics.

contexts.stem: The university awards funding to its most promising ___.
contexts.why: Scholars are high-achieving academic students or researchers.

contexts.stem: The ___ who draft education laws should consult teachers first.
contexts.why: Policymakers focus on the people who write rules and policy.

contexts.stem: It is ___ that the government acts immediately to stop the oil leak.
contexts.why: Imperative is strong and formal and signals urgency.

contexts.stem: There has been a ___ rise in house prices, up 40% in two years.
contexts.why: Substantial describes a large amount or size.

contexts.stem: Setting ___ goals, such as reading ten pages a day, keeps learners motivated.
contexts.why: Attainable means able to be reached.

contexts.stem: Because of its high cost, the project is not commercially ___.
contexts.why: Viable means capable of working successfully, often in business.

contexts.stem: Smartphones have become ___ in modern life: you see them on every street.
contexts.why: Ubiquitous means present everywhere.

contexts.stem: Power cuts are a ___ occurrence in the region, happening most weeks.
contexts.why: Frequent means happening often. Ubiquitous is about being everywhere.

contexts.stem: After the new trade law, the port city became ___ and its people grew wealthy.
contexts.why: Prosperous describes financial success.

contexts.stem: The two-day workshop was ___: the teams produced several practical ideas.
contexts.why: Fruitful means it produced good results.

contexts.stem: The central bank raised interest rates as part of its ___ policy.
contexts.why: Monetary relates to a country's money supply.

contexts.stem: Whether a painting is beautiful is highly ___.
contexts.why: Subjective means based on personal feelings, not facts.

contexts.stem: The charity ran a ___ campaign reaching every region of the country.
contexts.why: Nationwide means extending across the whole nation.

contexts.stem: ___ flights are cheaper than international ones.
contexts.why: Domestic means inside the country, as opposed to foreign or international.

contexts.stem: A corner shop and a family bakery are examples of small ___.
contexts.why: Businesses is the general term. Corporations are typically large.

contexts.stem: Multinational ___ such as car makers and oil giants have enormous influence.
contexts.why: Corporations are typically large companies.

contexts.stem: Driving ___ must be patient and clear.
contexts.why: Instructors teach practical skills such as driving.

contexts.stem: Many families hire private ___ to help with exam preparation.
contexts.why: Tutors teach individuals or small groups.

contexts.stem: The government must invest in public ___ so everyone can see a doctor.
contexts.why: Healthcare is the system of medical services. Well-being is a person's state.

contexts.stem: Meditation can improve mental ___.
contexts.why: Well-being covers mental and social health, not only the body.

contexts.stem: Basic human rights should be ___, applying to every person everywhere.
contexts.why: Universal means applying to everyone and everywhere.

contexts.stem: Cooperation between several governments is called ___ cooperation.
contexts.why: International involves two or more nations.

contexts.stem: Villages often share ___ wells and meeting halls.
contexts.why: Communal means shared by a group or community.

contexts.stem: Rapid change is shaping ___ attitudes towards ageing.
contexts.why: Societal is a formal adjective relating to society as a whole.

contexts.stem: Voting and jury service are part of our ___ duty.
contexts.why: Civic relates to citizens' duties in a city or state.

contexts.stem: The ___ watch scheme helped to reduce burglary on our street.
contexts.why: Neighbourhood is specific to a residential area.

contexts.stem: In a bygone ___, families gathered for dinner every night.
contexts.why: An era is a distinct period in history.

contexts.stem: Philosophers debate the meaning of human ___.
contexts.why: Existence is the formal, philosophical word.

contexts.stem: Researchers collected raw ___ from 2,000 households.
contexts.why: Data usually means raw facts and figures.

contexts.stem: Reading widely is a good way to build general ___.
contexts.why: Knowledge is information that has been understood and organised.

contexts.stem: The scientists want to ___ their method by adjusting small details.
contexts.why: Refine means improve through small changes.

contexts.stem: Schools should ___ a love of reading from an early age.
contexts.why: Foster means to encourage something to grow.

contexts.stem: The council will ___ a new recycling scheme next year.
contexts.why: Establish means to set something up.

contexts.stem: Prices of basic foods continue to ___.
contexts.why: Rise has no object. Raise and boost need one (raise prices).

contexts.stem: Some critics ___ that homework does more harm than good.
contexts.why: Contend is a formal verb for putting forward an argument.

contexts.stem: A large ___ of people attended the rally.
contexts.why: Use 'a large number of' with countable nouns such as people.

contexts.stem: A large ___ of water was wasted during the drought.
contexts.why: Use 'a large amount of' with uncountable nouns such as water.

contexts.stem: Scientists warn that fragile coral reef ___ are collapsing.
contexts.why: An ecosystem is a specific network of living things.

contexts.stem: The pyramids were built by an ancient ___.
contexts.why: Civilisation refers to whole cultures across history.

contexts.stem: Laws protect ___ from signing binding contracts before the age of 18.
contexts.why: Minors is the formal, legal term.

contexts.stem: A ___ weapon in the fight against poverty is education.
contexts.why: Potent means powerful, with a strong effect.

contexts.stem: The class includes students from ___ cultural backgrounds.
contexts.why: Diverse emphasises a wide range of distinct types.

contexts.stem: Keep spare batteries ___ in case of an emergency.
contexts.why: On hand means present and ready for use.

contexts.stem: The ___ view among economists is that growth will slow this year.
contexts.why: Prevailing means existing at a particular time, current.

contexts.stem: Obesity is increasingly ___ among teenagers.
contexts.why: Prevalent means widespread. Popular means liked, which changes the meaning.

contexts.stem: ___ art often explores social issues rather than traditional beauty.
contexts.why: Contemporary is the formal alternative to modern.

contexts.stem: Solar farms ___ electricity from sunlight.
contexts.why: Generate is used for electricity, income and jobs.

contexts.stem: Every ___ has rights, but also a duty to respect the law.
contexts.why: Citizen stresses a person's role within a state.

contexts.stem: Free school meals ___ children from poorer families to concentrate.
contexts.why: Assist is the formal alternative to help.

contexts.stem: She has deep ___ in renewable energy after twenty years in the field.
contexts.why: Expertise means a high level of skill and knowledge.

paragraphs.title: Education
paragraphs.text: Many people think that education is important. Good teachers help students to learn different skills. The government should provide more money for local schools. It is also important for children to get experience before they start work.
paragraphs.model: Numerous citizens regard schooling as crucial. Dedicated educators assist learners in acquiring diverse competencies. The state should supply additional funding for neighbourhood schools, and it is vital for youngsters to gain practical knowledge before they enter employment.

paragraphs.title: Environment
paragraphs.text: Climate change is a global problem and many people do not understand it. Companies should create green products, and the government should increase taxes on pollution. This can help the environment and improve life in modern society.
paragraphs.model: Climate change is a worldwide problem that numerous individuals fail to grasp. Corporations should generate greener products, while policymakers should raise taxes on pollution. This could protect the planet and enhance contemporary lifestyles.

paragraphs.title: Technology
paragraphs.text: Technology has changed modern life. Many adults use social media every day to share information. This is good for communication, but it can also have a bad effect on family time.
paragraphs.model: Technological progress has transformed contemporary existence. A large number of mature individuals use social media daily to share data. This is beneficial for communication, but it can also harm the household's leisure hours.

paragraphs.title: Health
paragraphs.text: Health is a personal matter, but the public also has a role. The government needs to provide better health services and increase funding. It is necessary to teach children about food. Many people believe this is possible and effective.
paragraphs.model: Well-being is a private matter, but the community also has a role. The authorities must supply better healthcare and raise funding. It is imperative to teach youngsters about nutrition. Numerous individuals contend that this is feasible and productive.

paragraphs.title: Work and economy
paragraphs.text: Work is important for economic growth. Companies develop new skills and create jobs. Many different experts believe that it is possible to improve the local economy if people have more time and information.
paragraphs.model: Employment is vital for economic growth. Corporations cultivate new competencies and generate jobs. A large number of diverse experts argue that it is feasible to enhance the regional economy if individuals have more leisure hours and data.

paragraphs.title: Community life
paragraphs.text: Community life is changing in many local areas. Social media helps people stay in touch, but family members spend less free time together. The government should help communities by providing public spaces.
paragraphs.model: Community life is changing in numerous neighbourhoods. Social media supports individuals in staying in touch, but household members spend fewer leisure hours together. The state should assist communities by supplying civic spaces.

prompts.q: The percentage of overweight children in western society has increased by almost 20% in the last ten years. Discuss the causes and effects of this disturbing trend.
Many men and women are making the decision to have children later in life. Why is this trend occurring? What are the impacts of this development on both family and society?
Stress is now a major problem in many countries around the world. What are some of the factors in modern society that cause this stress, and how can we reduce it?
Many museums and historical sites are mainly visited by tourists rather than local people. Why is this? What can be done to encourage local people to visit museums and historical sites?
Overpopulation of urban areas has led to numerous problems. Identify one or two serious ones and suggest ways that governments and individuals can tackle these problems.
Do the dangers derived from the use of chemicals in food production and preservation outweigh the advantages?

Many old buildings protected by law are part of a nation’s history. Some people think they should be knocked down and replaced by new ones. How important is it to maintain old buildings? Should history stand in the way of progress?

Nowadays the way many people interact with each other has changed because of technology. In what ways has technology affected the types of relationships people make? Is this a positive or negative development?

Some people believe that unpaid community service should be a compulsory part of high school programmes (for example, working for a charity, improving the neighborhood or teaching sports to younger children). To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Governments should spend more money on education than on recreation and sports. Do you agree or disagree?

Giving lectures in auditoriums to large numbers of students is an old way of teaching. With the technology available today there is no justification for it, and everything should be done online. To what extent do you agree or disagree? Give your own opinion.

Some people say that the best way to improve public health is by increasing the number of sports facilities. Others, however, say that this would have little effect on public health and that other measures are required. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Some people think that students who achieve the best academic results should be rewarded. Others believe it is more important to reward students who show improvement. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

In some countries the average weight of people is increasing and their levels of health and fitness are decreasing. What do you think are the causes of these problems and what measures could be taken to solve them?
The best way to understand other cultures is to work for a multinational organisation. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Currently there is a trend towards the use of alternative forms of medicine. However, at best these methods are ineffective, and at worst they may be dangerous. To what extent do you agree with this statement?

Air traffic is increasingly leading to more noise, pollution, and airport constuction. One reason for this is the growth in low-cost passenger flights, often to holiday destinations. Some people say that government should try to reduce air traffic by taxing it more heavily. Do you agree or disagree?
Smoking not only harms the smoker, but also those who are nearby. Therefore, smoking should be banned in public places. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Some people believe that they should be able to keep all the money they earn, and should not have to pay tax to the state. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Some people believe the aim of university education is to help graduates get better jobs. Others believe there are much wider benefits of university education for both individuals and society. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

Some people think that the main factors influencing a child’s development these days are things such as television, friends, and music. Others believe that the family still remains more important. Discuss both opinions and give your opinion.

Some people prefer to provide help and support directly to those in need. Others however prefer to give money to national and international charitable organisations. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
